Quick answer

To use Google Forms, sign in to forms.google.com, click the blank form template, add questions using the right-side toolbar, customize the theme, click Send to share, and review responses in the Responses tab. The full guide below walks through 12 sections: creating, customizing, adding question types, building sections, conditional logic, sharing, embedding, integrating with Sheets, collecting payments via add-ons, analyzing responses, troubleshooting, and when to switch.

Everything from creating your first form to advanced logic, integrations, and response analysis. Built for first-time users and growing teams.

To use Google Forms, sign in to forms.google.com, click the blank form template, add questions using the right-side toolbar, customize the theme, click Send to share, and review responses in the Responses tab. The full guide below walks through 12 sections: creating, customizing, adding question types, building sections, conditional logic, sharing, embedding, integrating with Sheets, collecting payments via add-ons, analyzing responses, troubleshooting, and when to switch.

Create your first form in 6 steps

Cover the essential setup. The full guide later in the article goes into design, logic, and integrations.

  1. 1

    Sign in and pick a template (or start blank)

    Go to forms.google.com with your Google account. Use a template from the gallery or click the blank template to start fresh.

  2. 2

    Add a title and description

    Click the form title at the top, type your form name, then add a description below explaining what the form is for.

  3. 3

    Add questions one at a time

    Click the + icon on the right-side toolbar to add a question. Pick the question type (short answer, multiple choice, dropdown, etc.) and type the question text.

  4. 4

    Customize the theme

    Click the paint palette icon (top right), set a header image, theme color, background, and font style. Match your brand.

  5. 5

    Configure settings

    Click the gear icon to choose response collection options: collect email, limit one response per person, allow editing responses, etc.

  6. 6

    Send the form

    Click the Send button (top right) and choose how to share: email, link, or iframe embed code for a website.

## What is Google Forms? Google Forms is a free, easy-to-use tool from Google for creating online forms, surveys, and quizzes. It’s popular for gathering feedback, planning events, and organizing information because it’s simple and integrates well with other Google tools like Sheets and Drive. ## Use Cases for Google Forms * Surveys: Collect opinions, feedback, or preferences on different topics. * Quizzes & Tests: Used by teachers and trainers to create quick tests. * Event Registrations: Great for RSVP forms or sign-ups. * Job Applications: Useful for creating simple application forms. * Feedback Forms: Collects customer or employee feedback on services or events. ## Key Features of Google Forms * Question Types: Multiple choice, checkboxes, short answers, and more. * Response Tracking: Responses are automatically collected and can be viewed in Google Sheets. * Basic Customization: Add logos, images, and videos. * Branching Logic: Create basic paths based on responses. * Real-time Collaboration: Easily work with others to build or edit forms. * Free and Accessible: No cost to create or share forms. ## Limitations of Google Forms * Limited Design Options: Few customization options, making forms look basic and similar. * No Advanced Logic: Basic branching but lacks complex conditional logic options. * No Payment Integration: Can’t collect payments directly through the form. * Minimal Security Controls: Limited features for advanced security and user privacy. * Limited Question Types: Basic question types; lacks rating scales, ranking, and file upload features found in other tools. * Lack of Analytics: Google Forms lacks advanced form analytics, detailed reports, and automated insights. For deeper analysis, you’ll need third-party tools or manual data processing. ## Why Formester is a Better Google Forms Alternative? Formester offers more customization, advanced conditional logic, tons of AI features such as AI form generation and integrations, including secure payment options. With Formester - a no code online form builder, you can create professional-looking forms with more control, privacy, and a wider range of question types, ideal for businesses, agencies, and educators who need more than what Google Forms provides. Try it yourself! ## How to Make a Google Form Creating a Google Form is simple and only takes a few steps. Here’s a complete guide from start to finish: ### 1. Start Creating Your Form * Go to Google Forms and log in with your Google account. * Click on the “Blank” form option or choose a template to get started. ### 2. Add a Title and Description * At the top, click to enter a title for your form. * Add a short description underneath to let people know what the form is for. ### 3. Add Questions and Fields * Click on the “+” button on the right to add a question. * Choose your question type from options like multiple choice, short answer, paragraph, checkboxes, dropdown, etc. * Type your question and add answer choices (if applicable). * Use the “Duplicate” icon to quickly copy a question format, or the “Trash” icon to delete one. * Click “Required” to make any question mandatory. ### 4. Customize Your Form’s Look (Design) * Click on the “Customize Theme” icon (paint palette) at the top. * Choose a background color, theme color, and font style to match your preferences. * You can also add a header image, like a logo or banner, to make the form more personalized. ### 5. Preview Your Form * Click the “Preview” icon (eye) at the top to see how your form will look to users. * Check for any mistakes or missing fields and go back to make edits if needed. ### 6. Set Up Form Settings * Go to “Settings” (gear icon). * Choose settings like “Collect email addresses,” “Limit to 1 response,” and “Allow response editing” as needed. * For quizzes, turn on “Make this a quiz” to assign points to questions. ### 7. Publish or Share Your Form * When your form is ready, click on the “Send” button. * You can share the form link, email it directly, or click the “<>” icon to get the embed code to add it to a website. * To share on social media, simply copy the link and paste it into a post. ## How to Add Rating Scale in Google Form * Open your form, click on “+” to add a question. * Choose the "Linear Scale" option. * Set your scale (e.g., 1 to 5) and add labels for each end (e.g., “Poor” to “Excellent”). * Use this free Net Promoter Survey (NPS) template from Formester if you are trying to guage how satisfied your customers are with your product or service. ## How to Add Payment to Google Form * Google Forms doesn’t support payments directly. * Use a third party add on such as Payable Forms or a free online form builder with payment integration like Formester. ## How to Add PDF to Google Forms * Google Forms doesn’t allow direct PDF uploads. * Upload your PDF to Google Drive and share the link in the form with a paragraph field. ## How to Make Conditional Questions in Google Forms * Before creating conditions for each question, you need to create a new Section and add the field that you want to show based on the previous answer. * Click on the question, select "Go to section based on answer." Then select the next section you want to show for each option on that field. * Google Forms lack the ability to create advanced forms that can carry out calculations or show different outcomes based on the user’s response. * That’s why it’s wise to use a free form builder with advanced conditional logic such as Formester. You can highly complex forms with a simple prompt using its build conditional forms with AI feature. Try it yourself! ## How to Change Image on Google Form * Go to the header area, click on the image icon. * Upload or choose a new image for the form header. ## How to Design a Google Form * Use the "Customize Theme" option to change colors, fonts, and header image. Keep design simple for better readability. * If you are searching for a solution that allows you to create custom branding kits, so you don’t have to customize each form or survey, try Formester! ## How to Duplicate a Google Form * Open your Google Form, click on the three dots menu. * Select “Make a copy” to duplicate. ## How to Make a QR Code for a Google Form * Open your Google Form, copy the form link. * Use a QR code generator (like QR Code Generator) and paste the link to create a QR code. Learn more. ## How to Make Google Form Public * Open your form, click on "Settings." * Turn off “Restrict to users in [your organization]” so anyone can access it. ## How to Make an Anonymous Google Form * Don’t include fields for name or email. * In "Settings," turn off “Collect email addresses” to ensure responses are anonymous. ## How to Translate a Google Form * Manually translate each question by editing the form in your desired language. * For multiple languages, create separate forms for each. If you want to create multilingual forms that have auto translations, try using Formester It's free to use and has tons of easy to use features to create advanced forms or surveys. ## How to Connect Google Form to Google Sheet * Open your form, go to "Responses," then click on the Google Sheets icon. * Choose to create a new sheet or connect to an existing one. Learn more. If you want to integrate your forms or surveys with any app to automate your workflow I highly recommend using Formester. ## How to Link Google Calendar on Forms * Google Forms doesn’t have a direct calendar link feature. * Add a Google Calendar event link in the description or confirmation message. If you want to the respondents to schedule appointments with you try using Formester’s free appointment booking form templates. ## How to Lock a Google Form To stop responses, open the form, go to "Responses," and toggle off “Accepting responses.” ## How to Embed Google Form * Open your form, click on “Send,” then select the “<>” (embed) icon. * Copy the embed code and paste it into your website’s HTML. ## How to Limit Responses in Google Forms * Google Forms itself doesn’t offer a response limit. * Use a Google Forms add-on like “FormLimiter” to set limits. If you want clear control over how many people can submit, which places they can submit from, and when to close the online form or survey, use a free form builder with Form limiter feature such as Formester. ## How to Close a Google Form * Go to “Responses” and toggle off the “Accepting responses” option to stop further submissions. ## How to Remove an Email from Google Forms * In "Settings," uncheck “Collect email addresses.” * For existing responses, remove emails manually in the linked Google Sheet. ## How to Get Notification When Someone Fills Out Google Form * Open your form, go to “Responses” and click the three dots. * Select “Get email notifications for new responses.” With Formester you can also set up a conditional autoresponder which sends a specific email based on the respondent’s answers, or adds a delay to automated email responses. ## How to Save Google Forms Responses as PDF * Open the form’s responses in Google Sheets. * Print or export the sheet as a PDF from the File menu. ## How to Edit Responses in Google Form * Go to "Responses" > "Individual," select the response, and click “Edit response.” * This only works if you or the respondent have edit permissions.

Frequently asked questions

Common questions about this guide.

How do I use Google Forms for the first time?
Go to forms.google.com, sign in with your Google account, click the blank form template, type a title and description, add questions from the right-side toolbar, click Send to share, and review responses in the Responses tab.
Is Google Forms free?
Yes. Google Forms is free with any Google account. There are no paid tiers; advanced features come from add-ons or alternative form builders.
What can you do with Google Forms?
Create surveys, quizzes, registration forms, contact forms, feedback forms, RSVP forms, event signups, and order forms. Responses auto-save to Google Sheets and can trigger email notifications.
How do I share a Google Form?
Click the Send button (top right). Choose a sharing method: email, link, or embed code. You can shorten the link or restrict the form to people in your organization.
Can I customize the design of a Google Form?
Yes. Click the paint palette icon to change the header image, theme color, background color, and font style. Custom CSS is not supported; for full branding control, use a dedicated form builder.
How do I add conditional logic in Google Forms?
Use Go to section based on answer on multiple-choice or dropdown questions. Per-question conditional show/hide is not supported in Google Forms; you'd route between sections instead.
How do I see Google Forms responses?
Click the Responses tab in the form editor. View summary charts, individual responses, or click the Google Sheets icon to send all responses to a spreadsheet for analysis.
Can Google Forms collect payments?
Not natively. Use a third-party add-on like Payable Forms or send respondents to an external payment link after submission. For built-in payments, use Formester.
How do I embed a Google Form on a website?
Click Send, then the embed code icon, copy the iframe code, and paste it into your site. Most CMS platforms (WordPress, Wix, Squarespace) support iframe embeds.
How many responses can Google Forms handle?
There's no official response limit on Google Forms. For very large response sets (over 100,000), Google Sheets becomes the bottleneck before Google Forms does.
Can I use Google Forms offline?
No. Google Forms requires internet to submit responses. For offline data collection, use a dedicated form builder with offline mode.
What's the best alternative to Google Forms?
Formester, Typeform, Jotform, and SurveyMonkey all offer features Google Forms lacks (advanced conditional logic, custom branding, payments, AI form generation). Formester is the closest free + powerful match.
